designs.name: agentboard-progress-scoring
designs.title: AgentBoard Progress Scoring
designs.description: Assess multi-turn LLM agent progress by identifying achieved milestones, scoring overall progress, categorizing the agent environment, and noting partial progress observations.

designs.name: agentrewardbench-trajectory-scoring
designs.title: AgentRewardBench Trajectory Scoring
designs.description: Evaluate web agent trajectories by rating step-level quality across multiple dimensions, judging overall success, and identifying where automatic evaluators disagree with human judgment.

designs.name: aitw-mobile-trajectory-review
designs.title: AITW Mobile Trajectory Review
designs.description: Step-by-step review of Android device-control episodes in the style of Android in the Wild (AITW; Rawles et al., NeurIPS 2023). Each step shows the screen and the action taken (tap, scroll, type, system button, or status action), with tap coordinates rendered as a grounding marker; annotators judge each action's correctness and grounding against the natural-language instruction, then give an episode-level verdict. Complements agentic/androidworld-mobile-agent-eval: AndroidWorld is a live-environment benchmark, while AITW is a static corpus of human demonstrations.
designs.paper_reference: Rawles et al., NeurIPS 2023 Datasets & Benchmarks

designs.name: androidworld-mobile-agent-eval
designs.title: AndroidWorld: Mobile Agent Task Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluation of autonomous agents performing tasks in dynamic Android environments. Annotators assess task completion, identify interaction types and touch gestures, evaluate UI understanding, and describe mobile-specific issues across diverse Android apps.

designs.name: apibank-tool-call-review
designs.title: API-Bank Tool Call Review
designs.description: Per-call review of API (tool) calls in tool-augmented assistant dialogues, based on API-Bank (Li et al., EMNLP 2023). Every API call in a dialogue becomes a reviewable card showing the tool name and arguments; annotators judge whether the right API was chosen, whether the arguments are correct, and whether the calls occur in the right order, then rate whether the assistant's final response is grounded in the API execution results.

designs.name: bigcodebench-human-baseline
designs.title: BigCodeBench Human Baseline Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluate agent-generated code solutions for BigCodeBench tasks. Annotators assess correctness against test suites, rate task complexity, evaluate code quality, and provide notes on the solution approach.

designs.name: codeprm-code-process-reward
designs.title: CodePRM Code Process Reward
designs.description: Process reward annotation for step-by-step code generation with execution feedback. Annotators verify each incremental code generation step against problem requirements, check syntactic validity, and provide feedback informed by test execution results.

designs.name: codeultrafeedback-code-preference
designs.title: CodeUltraFeedback: Code Preference Evaluation
designs.description: Pairwise comparison of code responses with multi-dimensional quality rating. Annotators compare two code solutions to a programming task, select which is better, rate both on the five CodeUltraFeedback coding-preference dimensions (instruction following, readability, complexity, style, and explanation), then justify their preference.

designs.name: devbench-repo-eval
designs.title: DevBench Repository Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluate AI-generated repositories across the full software development lifecycle. Annotators rate architecture design, code quality, test coverage, documentation, and dependency management for generated projects.

designs.name: mast-failure-taxonomy
designs.title: MAST Failure Taxonomy
designs.description: Annotate multi-agent system traces to identify failure modes from the MAST taxonomy, rate severity, pinpoint the first failure step, and describe the failure mechanism.

designs.name: mind2web-web-agent-tasks
designs.title: Mind2Web: Web Agent Task Annotation
designs.description: Web agent task annotation. Annotators describe web navigation tasks, identify target HTML elements for each action step, and label the action type (click, type, select) needed to complete the task.

designs.name: multiagentbench-collaboration-scorecard
designs.title: MultiAgentBench Collaboration Scorecard
designs.description: Coordination-quality rating of multi-agent LLM runs, based on MultiAgentBench (Zhu et al., ACL 2025). Annotators read a full multi-agent run transcript and score its communication and planning on 5-point scales using the paper's own evaluation rubric, then check off which run milestones were reached. Complements agentic/whowhen-failure-attribution, which localizes a single decisive failure rather than rating overall collaboration quality.

designs.name: osworld-desktop-agent-eval
designs.title: OSWorld: Desktop Agent Task Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluation of multimodal agents performing open-ended tasks in real desktop environments. Annotators assess task success, identify OS-level actions, rate efficiency, and analyze failures across Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS environments.

designs.name: prm800k-step-verification
designs.title: PRM800K Step-by-Step Verification
designs.description: Step-by-step verification of math reasoning chains based on OpenAI's PRM800K dataset. Annotators mark each reasoning step as Correct, Neutral, or Incorrect, stopping at the first error found, then judge the final answer correctness and explain any errors.

designs.name: processbench-math-error-steps
designs.title: ProcessBench Earliest-Error Identification
designs.description: Earliest-error identification in step-by-step math solutions, based on ProcessBench (Zheng et al., ACL 2025). Annotators read a model-generated solution one step at a time and mark the earliest erroneous step, or confirm that all steps are correct. Complements agentic/prm800k-step-verification: PRM800K collects per-step ratings for training process reward models, while ProcessBench is a benchmark that asks only for the location of the first error.

designs.name: r-judge-agent-safety
designs.title: R-Judge: Agent Safety Risk Evaluation
designs.description: Safety risk evaluation of LLM agent interaction records across diverse risk scenarios. Given an agent interaction trajectory, annotators assign a binary safe/unsafe label, identify the applicable risk type, and write a risk description explaining the risk's origin, the agent's triggering behavior, and the resulting harm.

designs.name: refactorbench-multi-file-eval
designs.title: RefactorBench Multi-File Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluate multi-file refactoring operations generated by coding agents. Annotators assess whether refactorings preserve behavior, identify the types of refactoring applied, rate code improvement, and provide detailed review comments.

designs.name: swe-prm-coding-process-reward
designs.title: SWE-PRM Process Reward Labels for Coding Agents
designs.description: Step-level process reward dataset for coding agents from the SWE-PRM paper (Gandhi et al., 2025). The Potato config reproduces per-step correctness rating, error typing, and explanation over SWE-bench Verified traces.

designs.name: swebench-code-agent-eval
designs.title: SWE-bench: Code Agent Solution Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluation of code agent solutions to real GitHub issues. Annotators review code patches generated by AI agents, assess correctness, check test compatibility, and evaluate code quality.

designs.name: swebench-plus-patch-screening
designs.title: SWE-Bench+ Patch Screening
designs.description: Screen and compare model-generated patches against gold patches for SWE-Bench+ instances. Annotators evaluate correctness, identify specific issues, and compare model vs. gold solutions side-by-side.

designs.name: swebench-verified-validation
designs.title: SWE-bench Verified Issue Validation
designs.description: Manually validate GitHub issues from SWE-bench to ensure they are well-specified, have adequate test patches, and are solvable. Annotators review the issue description, test patch, and gold patch to determine quality of each benchmark instance.
designs.paper_reference: Chowdhury et al., "Introducing SWE-bench Verified", OpenAI (2024); based on SWE-bench (Jimenez et al., ICLR 2024, arXiv:2310.06770)

designs.name: tau-bench-agent-eval
designs.title: tau-bench Agent Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluate tool-agent-user interactions in customer service domains by judging task success, conversation quality, tool use correctness, and providing evaluation rationale.

designs.name: trajeval-staged-evaluation
designs.title: TrajEval Staged Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluate code agent trajectories decomposed into search, edit, and verification stages, rating quality of each stage and determining overall pass/fail verdict.

designs.name: visualwebarena-visual-agent-eval
designs.title: VisualWebArena: Visual Web Agent Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluation of multimodal web agents on visually grounded web tasks. Annotators assess task completion, visual grounding accuracy, and visual reasoning capabilities by reviewing screenshot sequences and agent trajectories.

designs.name: webarena-web-agent-eval
designs.title: WebArena: Realistic Web Agent Evaluation Benchmark
designs.description: WebArena is a reproducible, self-hosted web environment with 812 tasks for testing autonomous language agents. This Potato config has annotators score whether an agent's actions completed each task.

designs.name: whowhen-failure-attribution
designs.title: Who&When Multi-Agent Failure Attribution
designs.description: Failure attribution for LLM multi-agent systems, based on the Who&When dataset (Zhang et al., ICML 2025 Spotlight). Annotators read the failure log of a run that did not solve its query and produce the attribution triple: the single responsible agent, the decisive error step (indexed from 0), and a natural-language reason, plus a certainty flag for group discussion. Complements agentic/mast-failure-taxonomy: MAST categorizes HOW multi-agent systems fail, while Who&When attributes WHO failed and WHEN.

designs.name: audio-transcription
designs.title: Audio Transcription Review
designs.description: Review and correct automatic speech recognition transcriptions with waveform visualization.

designs.name: audiohate-speech-detection
designs.title: AudioHate - Audio Hate Speech Detection
designs.description: Audio hate speech detection with explanations. Annotators classify audio clips for hate speech presence, identify target groups, and note acoustic indicators such as tone, emphasis, and prosody (An et al., SIGDIAL 2024).
designs.task_name: AudioHate: Explainable Audio Hate Speech Detection

designs.name: clotho-audio-captioning
designs.title: Clotho Audio Captioning
designs.description: Audio captioning and quality assessment based on the Clotho dataset (Drossos et al., ICASSP 2020). Annotators write natural language captions for audio clips, rate caption accuracy on a Likert scale, and classify the audio environment.

designs.name: covost-speech-translation
designs.title: CoVoST 2 - Speech Translation Evaluation
designs.description: Speech translation quality evaluation based on the CoVoST 2 dataset (Wang et al., arXiv 2020). Annotators listen to source audio, review translations, label audio segments, and rate overall translation quality.

designs.name: displace-speaker-diarization
designs.title: DISPLACE 2024 - Speaker and Language Diarization
designs.description: Speaker and language diarization in multilingual conversational audio. Annotators mark speaker turn boundaries, identify speakers, and label the language of each segment in conversational environments (Kalluri et al., INTERSPEECH 2024).

designs.name: doreco-language-documentation
designs.title: DoReCo: Language Documentation Reference Corpus
designs.description: DoReCo is a cross-linguistic corpus of 53 spoken languages with over 100 hours of narrative speech transcribed and time-aligned at the word and phone levels. This Potato config reproduces its multi-tier ELAN annotation workflow.

designs.name: emobox-multilingual-speech-emotion
designs.title: EmoBox - Multilingual Speech Emotion Recognition
designs.description: Multilingual speech emotion recognition across multiple languages and corpora. Annotators classify emotional states in speech clips and rate emotional intensity, based on the EmoBox toolkit and benchmark (Ma et al., INTERSPEECH 2024).

designs.name: emotion-recognition
designs.title: Speech Emotion Recognition
designs.description: Classify emotional states from speech audio including happiness, sadness, anger, fear, and more.

designs.name: librispeech-transcription
designs.title: LibriSpeech - Audio Transcription and Quality Rating
designs.description: Audio transcription quality assessment based on the LibriSpeech corpus (Panayotov et al., ICASSP 2015). Annotators rate audio quality using a slider and classify audio segments by content type, supporting speech recognition research and dataset curation.
designs.task_name: LibriSpeech: Audio Transcription and Quality Rating

designs.name: miami-code-switching
designs.title: Miami Bangor Code-Switching Annotation
designs.description: Multi-tier annotation of Spanish-English bilingual speech for code-switching analysis. Annotators perform per-word language identification, mark code-switch boundaries and types, classify switch direction and utterance-level language dominance, and provide orthographic transcriptions -- all on parallel tiers aligned to the audio timeline (Deuchar & Parafita Couto, Bangor Miami Corpus, TalkBank).

designs.name: music-genre-classification
designs.title: Music Genre Classification
designs.description: Classify music clips into genres and subgenres with mood and instrumentation tags.

designs.name: podcastfillers-disfluency-tagging
designs.title: PodcastFillers Disfluency Tagging
designs.description: Per-segment tagging of filler words and other audio events on podcast audio with time-aligned transcripts, based on the PodcastFillers dataset (Zhu, Caceres, Salamon, Interspeech 2022). Annotators tag each transcript segment with the fillers (uh, um, you know, like, other) and non-filler events (breaths, laughter, agreement sounds, repetitions, music, noise, simultaneous speakers) they hear. Note: this config also enables inline transcript correction, a showcase extension beyond the paper's tagging-only protocol.

designs.name: speaker-diarization
designs.title: Speaker Diarization
designs.description: Identify and label different speakers in audio recordings with timestamp-based segment annotation.

designs.name: speech-accent-classification
designs.title: Speech Accent Classification
designs.description: Classify speaker accents from audio recordings and assess speech quality. Annotators identify regional accent type, accent strength, audio quality, and speech clarity, with optional transcription correction. Based on the Mozilla Common Voice multilingual speech corpus.

designs.name: speech-commands-recognition
designs.title: Google Speech Commands: Keyword Spotting Dataset
designs.description: Google Speech Commands is a corpus of one-second spoken-word audio clips for training keyword spotting models (Warden, 2018). This Potato config reproduces the task: annotators play each clip, label the spoken word, and rate audio quality.

designs.name: sporc-podcast-turn-annotation
designs.title: SPoRC Podcast Speaker-Role and Turn Annotation
designs.description: Speaker-role labeling and diarization validation for podcast episodes, based on the Structured Podcast Research Corpus (SPoRC). Annotators read diarized speaker turns as chat bubbles synced to the episode audio, label each turn's speaker as Host, Guest, or Neither following the paper's Prolific validation protocol, flag incorrect turn boundaries, rate overall diarization quality, and record the hosts' names.
designs.task_name: SPoRC Podcast Speaker-Role and Turn Annotation

designs.name: tobi-prosody-annotation
designs.title: ToBI Prosodic Annotation
designs.description: Multi-tier prosodic annotation following the Tones and Break Indices (ToBI) framework. Annotators label pitch accents, phrase accents, boundary tones, and break indices on speech utterances, producing a layered prosodic transcription aligned to the audio timeline (Silverman et al., ICSLP 1992).

designs.name: voicemos-quality-assessment
designs.title: VoiceMOS Challenge 2024 - Speech Quality Assessment
designs.description: Speech quality assessment using Mean Opinion Score (MOS). Annotators rate synthesized or processed speech on naturalness, intelligibility, and overall quality on 1-5 scales (Huang et al., IEEE SLT 2024).

designs.name: wavcaps-audio-captioning
designs.title: WavCaps - Audio Captioning
designs.description: Audio captioning - write natural language descriptions of audio content. Annotators listen to audio clips and write detailed captions describing all sounds, events, and acoustic scenes (Mei et al., IEEE TASLP 2024).

designs.name: alpacaeval-instruction-eval
designs.title: AlpacaEval: Instruction-Following Preference Evaluation
designs.description: Pairwise preference annotation for instruction-following language models. Annotators compare two model responses side by side, select their preferred response, indicate preference strength, and rate individual response quality across diverse instruction categories.

designs.name: arena-hard-auto
designs.title: Arena Hard Auto - LLM Pairwise Evaluation
designs.description: Pairwise evaluation of LLM responses on challenging prompts from the Arena Hard benchmark (Li et al., ICML 2025). Annotators compare two responses on a continuous scale and rate question difficulty.
designs.task_name: Arena Hard Auto - LLM Pairwise Evaluation

designs.name: big-bench-task-eval
designs.title: BIG-Bench Task Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluate language model responses on diverse reasoning tasks from the BIG-Bench benchmark. Annotators assess correctness, provide reasoning explanations, and rate confidence for model outputs across multiple task categories.

designs.name: chatbot-arena-pairwise-bws
designs.title: Chatbot Arena: Pairwise LLM Preference Evaluation
designs.description: Chatbot Arena collects human pairwise preference votes between anonymous LLM responses to rank models with a Bradley-Terry leaderboard. This Potato config reproduces the pairwise and best-worst scaling judgment task.
designs.task_name: Chatbot Arena: Pairwise Comparison with BWS

designs.name: donotanswer-safety-eval
designs.title: Do-Not-Answer: LLM Safety Refusal Dataset
designs.description: Do-Not-Answer is a dataset of 939 prompts a responsible LLM should decline, organized by a risk taxonomy of 5 areas and 12 harm types. This Potato config reproduces the response refusal-evaluation task.

designs.name: esa-mt-error-spans
designs.title: ESA: Error Span Annotation for Machine Translation
designs.description: Error span annotation for machine translation output. Annotators identify error spans in translations, classify error types (accuracy, fluency, terminology, style), and rate severity.
designs.task_name: ESA: Error Span Annotation for MT

designs.name: flask-skill-rubric-evaluation
designs.title: FLASK Skill-based Rubric Evaluation
designs.description: Fine-grained human evaluation of LLM responses based on FLASK (Fine-grained Language Model Evaluation based on Alignment Skill Sets) by Ye, Kim, Kim, Hwang, Kim, Jo, Thorne, Kim, and Seo (KAIST), ICLR 2024 Spotlight. The annotator reads an instruction, a reference answer, and a model response, then scores each instance-relevant alignment skill (of FLASK's 12, e.g., logical robustness, factuality, comprehension, harmlessness) from 1 to 5 against skill-specific rubrics, plus the instruction's difficulty level. Unlike this showcase's Prometheus rubric evaluation task — from the same KAIST group, where an LLM judge scores with a single instance-specific rubric — FLASK decomposes quality into a fixed skill set whose skill-specific rubrics are scored by both humans and models.
designs.paper_reference: Seonghyeon Ye, Doyoung Kim, Sungdong Kim, Hyeonbin Hwang, Seungone Kim, Yongrae Jo, James Thorne, Juho Kim, and Minjoon Seo. 2024. FLASK: Fine-grained Language Model Evaluation based on Alignment Skill Sets. In The Twelfth International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR 2024), Spotlight.

designs.name: godspeed-agent-perception
designs.title: Godspeed Questionnaire: AI Assistant Perception
designs.description: Applies the Godspeed Questionnaire Series, the standard human-robot interaction measurement instrument by Bartneck, Kulić, Croft, and Zoghbi (International Journal of Social Robotics, 2009), to conversational AI outputs. The respondent reads a user prompt and an AI assistant's recorded response, then rates the assistant on the instrument's published 5-point bipolar adjective pairs across five indices: Anthropomorphism, Animacy, Likeability, Perceived Intelligence, and Perceived Safety.
designs.paper_reference: Christoph Bartneck, Dana Kulić, Elizabeth Croft, and Susana Zoghbi. 2009. Measurement Instruments for the Anthropomorphism, Animacy, Likeability, Perceived Intelligence, and Perceived Safety of Robots. International Journal of Social Robotics, 1(1):71-81.

designs.name: gpqa-expert-qa
designs.title: GPQA - Graduate-Level Expert QA Evaluation
designs.description: Expert-level question answering evaluation on graduate-level science questions from the GPQA benchmark (Rein et al., COLM 2024). Questions span physics, chemistry, and biology, designed to be answerable only by domain experts.

designs.name: helm-model-card-display
designs.title: HELM - Model Card Display and Evaluation
designs.description: Model performance summary display and evaluation based on the HELM benchmark (Liang et al., TMLR 2023). Annotators review model cards summarizing performance across multiple metrics and rate overall model quality.
designs.task_name: HELM - Model Card Display and Evaluation

designs.name: humaneval-code-correctness
designs.title: HumanEval Code Correctness Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluation of code generation correctness based on the HumanEval benchmark (Chen et al., arXiv 2021). Annotators assess whether AI-generated code solutions are correct, provide code review comments, and rate code quality on a numeric scale.

designs.name: ifeval-instruction-following
designs.title: IFEval: Instruction-Following Evaluation Benchmark for LLMs
designs.description: IFEval is the instruction-following benchmark from Google Research with 541 prompts built around 25 verifiable instruction types (word counts, formatting, keywords, structure). Scored by prompt-level and instruction-level accuracy, strict and loose. Reproduce the labeling in Potato.

designs.name: image-captioning-eval
designs.title: Image Captioning Evaluation
designs.description: Rate AI-generated image captions for accuracy, level of detail, and hallucination.

designs.name: longeval-faithfulness
designs.title: LongEval: Faithfulness Evaluation for Long-Form Summarization
designs.description: LongEval is the EACL 2023 protocol for human evaluation of faithfulness in long-form summaries (Krishna et al.). This Potato config reproduces its fine-grained, clause-level faithfulness judgments against source documents.

designs.name: machine-translation-eval
designs.title: Machine Translation Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluate machine translation quality with adequacy and fluency ratings.

designs.name: mmlu-knowledge-eval
designs.title: MMLU Knowledge Evaluation
designs.description: Multiple-choice knowledge evaluation across diverse academic subjects, based on the Massive Multitask Language Understanding benchmark (Hendrycks et al., ICLR 2021). Annotators select the correct answer from four options and provide an explanation.

designs.name: mqm-mt-error-annotation
designs.title: MQM Machine Translation Error Annotation
designs.description: Expert MQM (Multidimensional Quality Metrics) error annotation for machine translation based on Freitag, Foster, Grangier, Ratnakar, Tan, and Macherey (TACL 2021). Professional translators mark error spans in MT output with document context, assigning each error a category/sub-category from a broad-coverage MQM hierarchy (Accuracy, Fluency, Terminology, Style, Locale convention, plus Other, Source error, and Non-translation) and a severity (Major, Minor, or Neutral). This is the full-taxonomy expert protocol; it complements evaluation/esa-mt-error-spans, the lighter-weight ESA protocol (Kocmi et al., WMT 2024) in which annotators mark untyped minor/major spans plus a scalar score.
designs.paper_reference: Markus Freitag, George Foster, David Grangier, Viresh Ratnakar, Qijun Tan, and Wolfgang Macherey. 2021. Experts, Errors, and Context: A Large-Scale Study of Human Evaluation for Machine Translation. Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 9:1460-1474.

designs.name: mt-bench-judge-consistency
designs.title: MT-Bench Judge Consistency Evaluation
designs.description: Multi-turn conversation evaluation for LLM judge consistency, based on MT-Bench (Zheng et al., NeurIPS 2023). Annotators compare two assistant responses in a pairwise setting, rate overall quality on a 1-10 Likert scale, and classify the conversation category.

designs.name: mtbench-llm-evaluation
designs.title: MT-Bench: Multi-Turn LLM Evaluation Benchmark
designs.description: MT-Bench is an 80-question multi-turn benchmark for rating LLM chat assistants with an LLM judge, from Zheng et al. (NeurIPS 2023). This Potato config reproduces its 1-10 single-answer grading.

designs.name: prometheus-rubric-evaluation
designs.title: Prometheus: Rubric-Based LLM Evaluation
designs.description: Prometheus is an open-source evaluator LM that scores a response against a user-defined rubric on a 1-5 scale and writes feedback. This Potato config reproduces that rubric scoring and feedback task for human annotators.

designs.name: question-answering
designs.title: Question Answering
designs.description: Annotate answer spans in text passages for reading comprehension tasks.

designs.name: rewardbench-reward-eval
designs.title: RewardBench - Reward Model Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluation of reward model preferences via pairwise comparison of chosen and rejected responses. Annotators judge which response is better across chat, chat hard, safety, and reasoning categories, and rate response quality on multiple dimensions.
designs.paper_reference: Lambert et al., Findings of NAACL 2025

designs.name: sorrybench-refusal-eval
designs.title: SORRY-Bench: LLM Safety Refusal Evaluation
designs.description: SORRY-Bench is a benchmark of 440 unsafe instructions across 44 fine-grained risk categories for judging whether LLMs refuse harmful requests. This Potato config reproduces its fulfill-vs-refuse rating task.

designs.name: text-summarization-eval
designs.title: Text Summarization Evaluation
designs.description: Rate the quality of AI-generated summaries on fluency, coherence, and faithfulness.

designs.name: visual-qa
designs.title: Visual Question Answering
designs.description: Answer questions about images for VQA dataset creation.

designs.name: wildbench-llm-eval
designs.title: WildBench - LLM Evaluation on Real-World Tasks
designs.description: Evaluation of LLM outputs on challenging real-world user queries from WildBench. Annotators compare two model responses via pairwise preference, rate overall quality on a Likert scale, and provide reasoning for their judgments.

designs.name: wmt15-relative-ranking
designs.title: WMT15 Relative Ranking of Machine Translations
designs.description: The classic WMT relative-ranking (RR) protocol for machine translation evaluation, from 'Findings of the 2015 Workshop on Statistical Machine Translation' by Bojar et al. (WMT 2015). The annotator sees a source sentence, a human reference translation, and the outputs of up to five anonymized MT systems in random order, and ranks the outputs from best to worst with ties allowed; the joint rankings are reduced to pairwise judgments and aggregated with TrueSkill into the official system ranking.
designs.paper_reference: Ondřej Bojar, Rajen Chatterjee, Christian Federmann, Barry Haddow, Matthias Huck, Chris Hokamp, Philipp Koehn, Varvara Logacheva, Christof Monz, Matteo Negri, Matt Post, Carolina Scarton, Lucia Specia, and Marco Turchi. 2015. Findings of the 2015 Workshop on Statistical Machine Translation. In Proceedings of the Tenth Workshop on Statistical Machine Translation, pages 1-46, Lisbon, Portugal.
designs.task_name: WMT15 Relative Ranking of Machine Translations

designs.name: bigearth-net
designs.title: BigEarthNet Remote Sensing Classification
designs.description: Multi-label land cover classification from Sentinel-2 imagery (Sumbul et al., IGARSS 2019). Classify satellite patches into 43 land cover classes following the CORINE taxonomy.

designs.name: dota-aerial
designs.title: DOTA Aerial Image Object Detection
designs.description: Oriented bounding box detection in aerial images (Xia et al., CVPR 2018). Detect 15 object categories with arbitrary orientations including planes, ships, vehicles, and sports facilities.

designs.name: xview
designs.title: xView Satellite Object Detection
designs.description: Large-scale overhead imagery object detection (Lam et al., arXiv 2018). Detect 60 object classes including vehicles, buildings, and infrastructure from satellite images.

designs.name: cub-200-birds
designs.title: CUB-200-2011: Fine-Grained Bird Species Dataset
designs.description: CUB-200-2011 is a fine-grained bird image dataset of 11,788 photos across 200 species, each labeled with parts, attributes, and a bounding box (Wah et al., 2011). This Potato config reproduces the labeling task.

designs.name: imagenet
designs.title: ImageNet Image Classification
designs.description: Large-scale image classification following the ImageNet dataset (Deng et al., CVPR 2009). Classify images into 1000+ synsets organized according to the WordNet hierarchy.

designs.name: ms-coco
designs.title: MS COCO Object Detection & Categorization
designs.description: Object detection annotation following the MS COCO format (Lin et al., ECCV 2014). Select all object categories present in each image and mark object locations with bounding boxes, drawn from COCO's 80 common object categories.

designs.name: open-images
designs.title: Open Images Image Classification
designs.description: Large-scale image-level labeling following the Open Images dataset (Kuznetsova et al., IJCV 2020). Assign multi-label image-level tags across common object categories, and note occlusion, truncation, grouping, and visual relationships.

designs.name: pascal-voc
designs.title: PASCAL VOC Object Detection
designs.description: Multi-label object classification following the PASCAL Visual Object Classes challenge (Everingham et al., IJCV 2010). Tag which of the 20 VOC object categories are present in each image, with VOC-style difficulty, truncation, and occlusion attributes.

designs.name: places365
designs.title: Places365 Scene Classification
designs.description: Scene recognition and classification following the Places365 dataset (Zhou et al., TPAMI 2017). Classify images into 365 scene categories spanning indoor, outdoor, and natural environments.

designs.name: doclaynet-document-layout
designs.title: DocLayNet Document Layout Analysis
designs.description: Document layout analysis with bounding box annotations. Annotators draw bounding boxes around layout elements (text blocks, tables, figures, headers, footers, lists) in document page images.

designs.name: bdd100k
designs.title: BDD100K: Diverse Driving Dataset for Autonomous Driving
designs.description: BDD100K is a 100,000-video driving dataset from UC Berkeley (Yu et al., CVPR 2020) spanning detection, segmentation, lane marking, and tracking. This Potato config reproduces its driving-scene labeling tasks.

designs.name: kitti
designs.title: KITTI - 3D Object Annotation on Lidar Point Clouds
designs.description: Autonomous-driving benchmark from Geiger, Lenz and Urtasun (CVPR 2012). Annotators place oriented 3D cuboids on the lidar scan, with calibration projecting every box into the camera images for verification in 2D.

designs.name: flair-aerial-land-use
designs.title: FLAIR: French Land Cover from Aerospace Imagery
designs.description: Land use and land cover classification from high-resolution aerial imagery. Annotators classify the primary land use category of aerial image patches and identify any secondary land uses present. Based on the FLAIR dataset from the French National Institute of Geographic and Forest Information (IGN).

designs.name: t2i-compbench
designs.title: T2I-CompBench: Compositional Text-to-Image Benchmark
designs.description: T2I-CompBench is a 6,000-prompt benchmark for compositional text-to-image generation (Huang et al., NeurIPS 2023). This Potato config reproduces its human eval: Likert ratings, challenge-type tagging, and pairwise comparison.

designs.name: vitpose-keypoint-annotation
designs.title: ViTPose Human Keypoint Annotation
designs.description: Annotate human body keypoints and classify pose categories in images. Annotators place landmarks on visible anatomical joints using a simplified 13-point body model, draw bounding boxes around each person, and select the overall pose type. This is a generic keypoint-annotation template, not tied to a single published dataset.

designs.name: camelyon-pathology
designs.title: Camelyon17 - Breast Cancer Metastasis Detection in Pathology
designs.description: Pathology slide annotation for breast cancer metastasis detection. Based on the CAMELYON grand challenge (Ehteshami Bejnordi et al., JAMA 2017), annotators delineate tumor regions in whole-slide histopathology images and classify slides as positive or negative for metastasis.

designs.name: chexpert
designs.title: CheXpert Chest X-Ray Classification
designs.description: Multi-label classification of chest radiographs for 14 observations (Irvin et al., AAAI 2019). Annotate chest X-rays with pathology labels including uncertainty handling for clinical findings.

designs.name: mimic-cxr
designs.title: MIMIC-CXR Chest Radiograph Classification
designs.description: Large-scale chest radiograph classification based on MIMIC-CXR (Johnson et al., Scientific Data 2019). Multi-label classification with 14 observations derived from radiology reports.

designs.name: omnidocbench-document-parsing
designs.title: OmniDocBench Comprehensive Document Parsing
designs.description: Comprehensive document parsing annotation covering layout detection, text recognition, table structure, and formula recognition. Annotators draw bounding boxes and provide text transcriptions for document elements.

designs.name: sa1b-segment-anything
designs.title: Segment Anything (SA-1B) Interactive Segmentation
designs.description: Interactive image segmentation annotation. Annotators draw segmentation masks (polygons) and bounding boxes around all distinct objects in images, following the Segment Anything Model (SAM) annotation protocol.

designs.name: ade20k
designs.title: ADE20K: Scene Parsing and Semantic Segmentation Dataset
designs.description: ADE20K is a scene parsing dataset from MIT CSAIL (Zhou et al., CVPR 2017) with dense pixel labels for objects, stuff, and parts. This Potato config adapts it to an image-level category-tagging task over a curated subset of common ADE20K categories.

designs.name: cityscapes
designs.title: Cityscapes Instance Segmentation
designs.description: Urban scene understanding with instance-level semantic labeling (Cordts et al., CVPR 2016). Annotate street scenes with pixel-level labels for 30 classes across vehicles, humans, construction, and nature.

designs.name: lip-human-parsing
designs.title: LIP Human Parsing
designs.description: Pixel-level human body part segmentation (Gong et al., CVPR 2017). Parse human images into 19 semantic body-part and clothing labels including hair, face, arms, legs, and clothing items.
designs.paper_reference: Gong, Liang, Zhang, Shen & Lin, CVPR 2017

designs.name: celeba
designs.title: CelebA: Large-Scale Face Attributes Dataset
designs.description: CelebA is a face dataset of 202,599 celebrity images, each labeled with 40 binary attributes, identity, and 5 landmark points (Liu et al., ICCV 2015). This Potato config reproduces the 40-attribute multiselect task.

designs.name: deepfashion
designs.title: DeepFashion: Large-Scale Clothing Attributes Dataset
designs.description: DeepFashion is a clothes recognition and retrieval dataset of 800,000+ images labeled with 50 categories, 1,000 attributes, and landmarks (Liu et al., CVPR 2016). This Potato config reproduces its category and attribute task.

designs.name: docbank
designs.title: DocBank Document Layout Detection
designs.description: Document layout analysis benchmark (Li et al., COLING 2020). Detect and classify document elements including titles, abstracts, paragraphs, figures, tables, and captions.

designs.name: iwildcam
designs.title: iWildCam Wildlife Detection & Classification
designs.description: Camera trap image classification for wildlife monitoring (Beery et al., CVPR 2019). Classify wildlife species from camera trap images across diverse ecosystems worldwide.

designs.name: mvtec-ad
designs.title: MVTec AD Industrial Defect Detection
designs.description: Anomaly detection and localization in industrial images (Bergmann et al., CVPR 2019). Detect defects across 15 object and texture categories including metal nuts, transistors, and leather.

designs.name: wikiart
designs.title: WikiArt Artwork Classification
designs.description: Art classification by style, genre, and artist (Saleh & Elgammal, 2015). Classify paintings into artistic movements, genres, and predict artist attribution.

designs.name: pixmo-points-pointing
designs.title: PixMo-Points - Pointing Annotation for Vision-Language Models
designs.description: Collect the pointing supervision behind Molmo: place a point on what each referring expression refers to. Scored as a point-in-region hit rate, because a point has no area and every IoU against one is zero.

designs.name: refcoco-expression
designs.title: RefCOCO - Referring Expression Grounding
designs.description: Visual grounding task where annotators bind each referring expression to a region of the image. Based on RefCOCO (Yu et al., ECCV 2016), reproduced with Potato's grounding_eval schema, which scores grounding by IoU at four thresholds and counts ungroundedness separately.

designs.name: textvqa-reading-in-images
designs.title: TextVQA: Reading Text in Images for VQA
designs.description: TextVQA is a visual question answering dataset where reading scene text in the image is needed to answer. This Potato config reproduces the task: show an image and question, then collect a free-text answer.

designs.name: vqav2-visual-question-answering
designs.title: VQA v2.0: Visual Question Answering Dataset
designs.description: VQA v2.0 is a balanced visual question answering benchmark of open-ended questions over COCO images, with ~1.1M questions and 10 answers each (Goyal et al., CVPR 2017). This Potato config reproduces the answering task.

designs.name: wtw-table-structure-annotation
designs.title: WTW Wired Table Structure Annotation
designs.description: Cell-grid structure annotation for photographed and scanned wired tables, based on the WTW (Wired Table in the Wild) dataset (Long et al., ICCV 2021). Annotators set each table's row/column grid dimensions and mark every cell's logical role, including headers, empty cells, and spanned continuations of merged cells, then record which of WTW's seven challenging conditions apply and the image source. Pixel-level cell quadrilaterals from the full WTW protocol are deliberately out of scope.

designs.name: xbd-building-damage
designs.title: xBD: Building Damage Assessment from Satellite Imagery
designs.description: Building damage assessment from pre- and post-disaster satellite imagery. Annotators compare side-by-side satellite images to rate damage on the four-level Joint Damage Scale, identify building types, and note specific damage features. Based on the xBD dataset (CVPR Workshops 2019) behind the xView2 challenge.

designs.name: chartinfo-chart-analysis
designs.title: CHART-Infographics: Chart and Infographic Analysis
designs.description: Chart and infographic analysis with structured extraction. Annotators identify chart elements (axes, legends, data points, titles) with bounding boxes, classify chart types, and extract data values. Supports structured understanding of visual data representations.

designs.name: hatred-hateful-memes
designs.title: HatReD: Multi-Domain Hateful Meme Detection
designs.description: Hateful meme detection requiring understanding of both image and text. Annotators classify memes as hateful or not, identify the target of hate, and explain why the meme is hateful. Based on the HatReD dataset spanning multiple domains of online meme content.

designs.name: lerobot-episode-annotation
designs.title: LeRobot - Robot Episode Annotation
designs.description: Annotate teleoperated robot demonstrations: synchronized camera streams and per-frame arm signals on one timeline, with phase segmentation, outcome and failure cause, and a dense progress-reward curve.

designs.name: mmbench-multimodal-eval
designs.title: MMBench: Multimodal Vision-Language Benchmark
designs.description: MMBench is a multiple-choice benchmark of about 2,974 questions testing vision-language models across 20 ability dimensions (Liu et al., ECCV 2024). This Potato config reproduces image-question answering with skill tagging.

designs.name: mmmu-multimodal-understanding
designs.title: MMMU: Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding
designs.description: Multi-discipline multimodal QA requiring college-level understanding. Annotators answer multiple-choice questions that require interpreting images (charts, diagrams, photos) along with text across 30 subjects spanning STEM, humanities, social sciences, and more.

designs.name: mocheg-multimodal-factcheck
designs.title: MOCHEG: Multimodal Fact-Checking with Explanations
designs.description: Multimodal fact-checking requiring reasoning over both text and images. Annotators verify claims using multimodal evidence, identify relevant spans in text evidence, and provide explanations for their verdicts. Based on the MOCHEG dataset (Yao et al., SIGIR 2023).

designs.name: rt2-robotic-action-annotation
designs.title: RT-2 - Robotic Action Annotation
designs.description: Robotic manipulation task evaluation and action segmentation based on RT-2 (Brohan et al., CoRL 2023). Annotators evaluate task success, describe actions, rate execution quality, and segment video into action phases.

designs.name: saycan-robot-planning
designs.title: SayCan: Grounding Language in Robotic Affordances
designs.description: SayCan grounds a large language model in learned robot skills so a robot can carry out long-horizon natural-language instructions. This Potato config reproduces the human evaluation of its generated action plans.

designs.name: scienceqa-multimodal-reasoning
designs.title: ScienceQA Multimodal Reasoning
designs.description: Multimodal science question answering with chain-of-thought reasoning, based on ScienceQA (Lu et al., NeurIPS 2022). Annotators answer multiple-choice science questions that may include images, provide chain-of-thought explanations, and categorize the science domain.

designs.name: soda-eval-social-dialogue
designs.title: SODA: Social Dialogue Quality Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluate the quality of socially-grounded dialogues generated through social commonsense contextualization. Annotators rate naturalness, coherence, social appropriateness, and commonsense alignment of dialogues situated in specific social contexts and interpersonal relationships.
designs.paper_reference: Mendonca et al., Findings of EMNLP 2024

designs.name: alpacafarm-simulation
designs.title: AlpacaFarm Preference Simulation
designs.description: Simulate human preferences for instruction-following responses. Create preference data for efficient RLHF research and LLM evaluation.

designs.name: beavertails-safety-preference
designs.title: BeaverTails Safety Preference
designs.description: Annotate AI responses for safety across multiple harm categories. Identify unsafe content and rate response quality for building safer AI systems.

designs.name: constitutional-ai-harmlessness
designs.title: Constitutional AI Harmlessness Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluate AI assistant responses for harmlessness and helpfulness based on the Constitutional AI framework by Anthropic. Annotators rate responses on a harmfulness scale, assess helpfulness, and provide explanations for their judgments.

designs.name: dpo-preference-data
designs.title: DPO Preference Data Collection
designs.description: Pairwise preference annotation for Direct Preference Optimization, based on Rafailov et al., NeurIPS 2023. Annotators compare two model responses to a prompt, select a preference, rate alignment dimensions, and provide reasoning.

designs.name: helpsteer-multiattribute-rating
designs.title: HelpSteer Multi-Attribute Rating
designs.description: Multi-dimensional response quality rating for reward model training. Annotators rate AI responses on 5 attributes: helpfulness, correctness, coherence, complexity, and verbosity using a 0-4 scale.

designs.name: hh-rlhf-pairwise-preference
designs.title: HH-RLHF Pairwise Preference
designs.description: Classic pairwise preference annotation for helpfulness and harmlessness. The foundational RLHF dataset format where annotators choose between 'chosen' and 'rejected' responses.

designs.name: instructgpt-preference
designs.title: InstructGPT Instruction Following
designs.description: Evaluate how well AI responses follow user instructions. Compare outputs on helpfulness, truthfulness, and harmlessness for RLHF training.

designs.name: mmlu-pro-tiered-eval
designs.title: MMLU-Pro - Tiered Multi-Subject Evaluation
designs.description: Tiered evaluation for multi-subject question answering, based on MMLU-Pro (Wang et al., NeurIPS 2024). Annotators verify answers to challenging 10-option multiple choice questions across STEM and humanities subjects, using a tiered annotation scheme for topic and subtopic categorization.

designs.name: oasst-conversation-quality
designs.title: OpenAssistant Conversation Quality
designs.description: Rate AI assistant responses across multiple quality dimensions. Evaluate conversations for the OpenAssistant crowdsourced dataset.

designs.name: pairwise-preference-rationale
designs.title: Pairwise Preference with Rationale
designs.description: Compare two AI responses and select the better one while providing a written justification. Used for reward model training with interpretable preference signals.

designs.name: redteam-adversarial-eval
designs.title: Red Team Adversarial Evaluation
designs.description: Evaluate AI responses to adversarial prompts. Assess whether the model was successfully attacked and rate the severity of any harmful outputs.

designs.name: rewardbench-reward-model-eval
designs.title: RewardBench: Reward Model Evaluation via Pairwise Preference
designs.description: Reward model evaluation through pairwise preference annotation. Annotators choose between a 'chosen' (better) and 'rejected' (worse) response across RewardBench's four categories (chat, chat hard, safety, reasoning).

designs.name: saferlhf-dual-preference
designs.title: SafeRLHF Dual-Dimension Preference
designs.description: Safety-aware preference annotation with separate judgments for helpfulness and harmlessness. Includes safety category labeling across 19 harm types for constrained AI alignment.
designs.paper_reference: Dai et al., ICLR 2024 (Safe RLHF); dataset: PKU-SafeRLHF (Ji et al.)

designs.name: spin-self-play
designs.title: SPIN Self-Play Preference Annotation
designs.description: Human vs. AI response discrimination for Self-Play Fine-Tuning, based on Chen et al., ICML 2024. Annotators identify which of two responses was written by a human versus an AI model, and rate the fluency of both responses.

designs.name: summary-preference-comparison
designs.title: Summary Preference Comparison
designs.description: Pairwise comparison of text summaries with axis-based quality ratings. Annotators select preferred summaries and rate them on accuracy, coverage, and coherence for reward model training.

designs.name: ultrafeedback-multiaspect
designs.title: UltraFeedback: Fine-Grained AI Preference Dataset
designs.description: UltraFeedback is a 64k-prompt preference dataset where GPT-4 rates model responses on four aspects (Cui et al., ICML 2024). This Potato config reproduces the multi-aspect 1-5 rating workflow.

designs.name: ultrafeedback-rubric-evaluation
designs.title: UltraFeedback Rubric Evaluation
designs.description: Fine-grained response evaluation across 4 dimensions with written rationales. Rate responses on helpfulness, honesty, instruction-following, and truthfulness using detailed rubrics.

designs.name: webgpt-comparison
designs.title: WebGPT Answer Comparison
designs.description: Compare answers with and without web search access. Evaluate whether web-augmented responses are more accurate, helpful, and well-sourced.

designs.name: task09-drug-drug-interactions
designs.title: Drug-Drug Interaction Extraction from Biomedical Texts
designs.description: Extract drug entities and classify drug-drug interactions from biomedical texts, based on SemEval-2013 Task 9 (Segura-Bedmar et al.). Annotators identify drug mentions by type and classify interaction relationships between drug pairs.

designs.name: task04-absa-original
designs.title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (Original ABSA)
designs.description: Identify aspect terms in review text and classify their sentiment polarity, based on SemEval-2014 Task 4 (Pontiki et al.). Annotators highlight aspect terms and assign sentiment labels across restaurant and laptop review domains.

designs.name: task04-timeline-event-ordering
designs.title: TimeLine: Cross-Document Event Ordering
designs.description: Identify event mentions and temporal expressions in news text and classify temporal relations between events, based on SemEval-2015 Task 4 (Minard et al.). Annotators build timelines by ordering events related to a target entity across documents.

designs.name: task14-clinical-text-analysis
designs.title: Analysis of Clinical Text: Disorder Identification and Normalization
designs.description: Identify disorder mentions and their attributes in clinical discharge summaries, based on SemEval-2015 Task 14 (Elhadad et al.). Annotators mark disorder spans, body locations, severity indicators, and classify the assertion status of each disorder.

designs.name: task02-interpretable-sts
designs.title: Interpretable Semantic Textual Similarity
designs.description: Fine-grained semantic similarity assessment between sentence pairs with span alignment, combining chunk-level annotation with graded similarity scoring. Based on SemEval-2016 Task 2.

designs.name: task05-aspect-sentiment
designs.title: Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis
designs.description: Identification of aspect terms in review text with sentiment polarity classification for each aspect. Based on SemEval-2016 Task 5 (ABSA).

designs.name: task06-stance-detection
designs.title: Detecting Stance in Tweets
designs.description: Classification of stance expressed in tweets toward specific targets as favor, against, or neither. Based on SemEval-2016 Task 6 (Stance Detection).

designs.name: task07-sentiment-intensity
designs.title: Determining Sentiment Intensity of English and Arabic Phrases
designs.description: Determine the sentiment intensity of English and Arabic phrases using Best-Worst Scaling: annotators see four phrases at a time and select the most positive and most negative, which are aggregated into real-valued intensity scores in [0,1]. Based on SemEval-2016 Task 7.

designs.name: task10-minimal-semantic-units
designs.title: Detecting Minimal Semantic Units and Their Meanings (DiMSUM)
designs.description: Identification of multiword expression components in text through span annotation, detecting minimal semantic units that function as single meaning-bearing elements. Based on SemEval-2016 Task 10.

designs.name: task11-complex-word-identification
designs.title: Complex Word Identification
designs.description: Binary classification of words as complex or simple for text simplification purposes, identifying words that may be difficult for non-native speakers or people with reading difficulties. Based on SemEval-2016 Task 11.

designs.name: task12-clinical-tempeval
designs.title: Clinical TempEval - Temporal Information Extraction from Clinical Notes
designs.description: Extraction of temporal information from clinical text, identifying time expressions, event mentions, and their temporal relations. Based on SemEval-2016 Task 12 (Clinical TempEval).

designs.name: task02-word-similarity
designs.title: Multilingual Semantic Word Similarity
designs.description: Graded word similarity judgment across multiple languages, based on SemEval-2017 Task 2. Annotators rate how semantically similar two words are on a continuous scale, supporting cross-lingual evaluation of distributional semantic models.

designs.name: task03-community-qa
designs.title: Community Question Answering
designs.description: Answer quality classification for community forum question-answer pairs, based on SemEval-2017 Task 3. Annotators judge whether a given answer is good, potentially useful, or bad with respect to the original question.

designs.name: task05-financial-sentiment
designs.title: Fine-Grained Sentiment Analysis on Financial Microblogs and News
designs.description: Graded sentiment analysis of financial text with topic classification, rating market sentiment from very bearish to very bullish on a 7-point scale. Based on SemEval-2017 Task 5.

designs.name: task06-hashtagwars-humor
designs.title: #HashtagWars - Learning a Sense of Humor
designs.description: Humor ranking of tweets submitted to Comedy Central's @midnight #HashtagWars, classifying comedic quality. Based on SemEval-2017 Task 6.

designs.name: task07-pun-detection
designs.title: Detection and Interpretation of English Puns
designs.description: Detection of puns in text with identification of the specific pun word, combining binary classification with span annotation. Based on SemEval-2017 Task 7.
designs.task_name: Detection and Interpretation of English Puns

designs.name: task02-emoji-prediction
designs.title: Multilingual Emoji Prediction
designs.description: Prediction of the most likely emoji for a given tweet, choosing from the 20 most frequent emojis. Based on SemEval-2018 Task 2 (Multilingual Emoji Prediction).

designs.name: task03-irony-detection
designs.title: Irony Detection in English Tweets
designs.description: Fine-grained irony detection in tweets, distinguishing between verbal irony by polarity clash, situational irony, other verbal irony, and non-ironic content. Based on SemEval-2018 Task 3.

designs.name: task04-character-identification
designs.title: Character Identification on Multiparty Dialogues
designs.description: Identification and linking of character mentions in TV show dialogue, combining span annotation with entity resolution for the main cast of Friends. Based on SemEval-2018 Task 4.

designs.name: task05-event-counting
designs.title: Counting Events and Participants in News
designs.description: Counting the number of events or incidents described in news reports and providing event descriptions. Based on SemEval-2018 Task 5 (Counting Events and Participants).
designs.task_name: Counting Events and Participants in News

designs.name: task06-time-normalization
designs.title: Parsing Time Normalizations
designs.description: Parsing time expressions in text using the SCATE (Semantically Compositional Annotation of Time Expressions) schema, marking typed time entities and operators (e.g., Year, Month-Of-Year, Day-Of-Month, Last, Next, This, Between) that compose into interval semantics. Based on SemEval-2018 Task 6.

designs.name: task07-scientific-relations
designs.title: Semantic Relation Extraction and Classification in Scientific Papers
designs.description: Extraction and classification of semantic relations between entities in scientific abstracts, covering six relation types. Based on SemEval-2018 Task 7.
designs.task_name: Semantic Relation Extraction in Scientific Papers

designs.name: task08-cybersecurity-ner
designs.title: SecureNLP - Malware Report Semantic Extraction
designs.description: Semantic extraction from cybersecurity (APT malware) reports, following SemEval-2018 Task 8 (SecureNLP) on the MalwareTextDB corpus: classify whether a sentence is relevant to malware actions/capabilities, then tag tokens with the Action / Entity / Modifier labels and assign MAEC attribute categories to Action tokens.

designs.name: task09-hypernym-discovery
designs.title: Hypernym Discovery
designs.description: Discovery of hypernyms (broader terms) for a given target term in context, with classification of the hypernym relationship type. Based on SemEval-2018 Task 9.

designs.name: task10-discriminative-attributes
designs.title: Capturing Discriminative Attributes
designs.description: Binary classification of whether a semantic attribute discriminates between two words, testing understanding of fine-grained word meaning differences. Based on SemEval-2018 Task 10.

designs.name: task11-commonsense-comprehension
designs.title: Machine Comprehension Using Commonsense Knowledge
designs.description: Multiple-choice reading comprehension requiring commonsense reasoning over narrative texts, selecting the best answer and providing reasoning. Based on SemEval-2018 Task 11.

designs.name: task03-emocontext
designs.title: EmoContext - Contextual Emotion Detection in Text
designs.description: Contextual emotion detection in 3-turn conversations, classifying the emotion of the final turn given conversational context. Based on SemEval-2019 Task 3 (EmoContext).

designs.name: task04-hyperpartisan-news
designs.title: Hyperpartisan News Detection
designs.description: Binary classification of news articles as hyperpartisan or not, detecting extreme one-sided political bias. Based on SemEval-2019 Task 4 (Hyperpartisan News Detection).

designs.name: task05-hateval
designs.title: HatEval - Multilingual Detection of Hate Speech Against Immigrants and Women
designs.description: Detection and classification of hate speech targeting immigrants and women on Twitter, including fine-grained annotation of target range (individual vs. generic) and aggressiveness. Based on SemEval-2019 Task 5 (HatEval).

designs.name: task08-fact-checking-cqa
designs.title: Fact-Checking in Community Question Answering Forums
designs.description: Verification of factual claims in community question answering forums, classifying answers to factual questions as true, false, or non-factual. Based on SemEval-2019 Task 8 (Fact-Checking in CQA), Subtask B.

designs.name: task09-suggestion-mining
designs.title: Suggestion Mining from Online Reviews and Forums
designs.description: Binary classification of sentences as suggestions or non-suggestions in online reviews and forum posts. Based on SemEval-2019 Task 9 (Suggestion Mining).

designs.name: task10-math-qa
designs.title: Math Question Answering and Category Classification
designs.description: Answering SAT-style mathematical questions with category classification, covering closed-vocabulary algebra, open-vocabulary algebra, and geometry. Based on SemEval-2019 Task 10 (Math QA).

designs.name: task12-toponym-resolution
designs.title: SemEval-2019 Task 12: Toponym Resolution in Scientific Papers
designs.description: SemEval-2019 Task 12 covers toponym detection and resolution in scientific text: finding place-name mentions and linking them to GeoNames locations. Task overview, paper and dataset links, and a Potato span-annotation config to replicate it.

designs.name: task02-lexical-entailment
designs.title: Predicting Multilingual and Cross-Lingual Lexical Entailment
designs.description: Rate the degree to which one word (X) is a type of another word (Y) — graded lexical entailment (hyponymy/is-a) — based on SemEval-2020 Task 2 (Glavaš et al.). Covers multilingual and cross-lingual graded lexical entailment derived from HyperLex.
designs.task_name: Predicting Multilingual and Cross-Lingual Lexical Entailment

designs.name: task03-graded-word-similarity
designs.title: Graded Word Similarity in Context
designs.description: Rate the graded semantic similarity of a PAIR of target words that appear together within a shared context, based on SemEval-2020 Task 3 (Armendariz et al.). The same word pair is judged within two different contexts; Subtask 1 predicts the change in similarity between contexts and Subtask 2 predicts the absolute rating. Ratings follow the SimLex-style 0-6 similarity scale (later mapped to 0-10). Similarity is distinct from relatedness (e.g., coffee and cup are related but not similar).

designs.name: task04-commonsense-validation
designs.title: Commonsense Validation and Explanation
designs.description: Determine which of two sentences makes sense and which does not based on commonsense knowledge, then provide a natural language explanation, based on SemEval-2020 Task 4 (Wang et al.).

designs.name: task05-counterfactual
designs.title: Counterfactual Detection and Reasoning
designs.description: Detect counterfactual statements and annotate their antecedent and consequent spans, based on SemEval-2020 Task 5 (Yang et al.). Annotators identify whether a statement describes a hypothetical situation counter to known facts.

designs.name: task06-defteval-definitions
designs.title: DeftEval - Extracting Definitions from Free Text
designs.description: Detect whether a sentence contains a definition and extract term, definition, qualifier, and alias spans from textbook and legal text, based on SemEval-2020 Task 6 (Spala et al.).
designs.task_name: DeftEval - Extracting Definitions from Free Text

designs.name: task07-humor-headlines
designs.title: Assessing Humor in Edited News Headlines
designs.description: Rate the funniness of edited news headlines on a 0-3 scale and judge which of two edited versions is funnier, based on SemEval-2020 Task 7 (Hossain et al.). Headlines are minimally edited by replacing a single word to create humorous effect.
designs.task_name: Assessing Humor in Edited News Headlines

designs.name: task08-memotion-memes
designs.title: Memotion Analysis - Sentiment and Type Classification of Memes
designs.description: Classify the overall sentiment of internet memes and identify their communicative types (sarcastic, humorous, offensive, motivational), based on SemEval-2020 Task 8 (Sharma et al.). Annotators analyze both text and image descriptions of memes.
designs.task_name: Memotion Analysis - Sentiment and Type Classification of Memes

designs.name: task09-code-mixed-sentiment
designs.title: SemEval-2020 Task 9: Code-Mixed Sentiment (SentiMix)
designs.description: SentiMix is the SemEval-2020 Task 9 benchmark for sentence-level sentiment on code-mixed tweets, covering Hindi-English and Spanish-English. This Potato config reproduces its positive/negative/neutral labeling.
designs.task_name: Sentiment Analysis for Code-Mixed Social Media Text

designs.name: task10-emphasis-selection
designs.title: Emphasis Selection for Written Text
designs.description: Select words or phrases in short written text that should be emphasized (e.g., bolded or highlighted) to convey the author's intended meaning most effectively, based on SemEval-2020 Task 10 (Shirani et al.).

designs.name: task01-lexical-complexity
designs.title: Lexical Complexity Prediction
designs.description: Predict the complexity of words in context using both Likert scale and continuous slider ratings, based on SemEval-2021 Task 1 (Shardlow et al.). Annotators assess how difficult a target word is for a non-native English speaker to understand.

designs.name: task02-crosslingual-wic
designs.title: Multilingual Word-in-Context
designs.description: Cross-lingual word sense disambiguation task where annotators determine whether a target word is used in the same sense across two different contexts, based on SemEval-2021 Task 2 (Martelli et al.).

designs.name: task03-multilingual-srl
designs.title: Multilingual Semantic Role Labeling
designs.description: Annotate predicate-argument structure in multilingual text by marking predicates, labeling their argument spans with semantic roles, and classifying voice type. Mirrors the topic of SemEval-2021 Task 3 (Span- and Dependency-based Multilingual and Cross-lingual Semantic Role Labeling); grounded in the UniteD-SRL dataset (Tripodi, Conia & Navigli, Findings of EMNLP 2021).
designs.paper_reference: Tripodi, Conia & Navigli, Findings of EMNLP 2021 (UniteD-SRL)

designs.name: task04-recam-abstract-meaning
designs.title: ReCAM - Reading Comprehension of Abstract Meaning
designs.description: Multiple-choice cloze-style reading comprehension requiring understanding of abstract concepts, based on SemEval-2021 Task 4 (Zheng et al.). Annotators select the best word to fill a blank in a passage from five abstract-concept options.
designs.task_name: ReCAM - Reading Comprehension of Abstract Meaning

designs.name: task06-persuasion-multimodal
designs.title: SemEval-2021 Task 6: Persuasion Techniques in Memes
designs.description: SemEval-2021 Task 6 labels persuasion techniques in 950 English memes across text, spans, and the full image. This Potato config reproduces the multiselect technique labeling and span marking.

designs.name: task07-hahackathon-humor
designs.title: SemEval-2021 Task 7: HaHackathon Humor Detection
designs.description: SemEval-2021 Task 7 (HaHackathon) detects whether a text is humorous and rates how offensive it is, using 10,000 tweets and short jokes. This Potato config reproduces the humor and offense annotation interface.
designs.task_name: HaHackathon - Detecting and Rating Humor and Offense

designs.name: task08-measeval
designs.title: MeasEval - Counts and Measurements
designs.description: Extract and classify measurements, quantities, units, and measured entities from scientific text, based on SemEval-2021 Task 8 (Harper et al.). Annotators span-annotate measurement components and classify quantity types with normalized values.

designs.name: task09-verification-tables
designs.title: Statement Verification and Evidence Finding with Tables
designs.description: Verify whether a natural language statement is entailed or refuted by tabular data and identify key evidence cells, based on SemEval-2021 Task 9 (Wang et al.). Annotators assess factual claims against structured table content.
designs.task_name: Statement Verification and Evidence Finding with Tables

designs.name: task11-nlpcontributiongraph
designs.title: NLPContributionGraph - Structured Extraction of NLP Contributions
designs.description: Extract structured contribution information from NLP papers by annotating research problem, approach, model, dataset, metric, and result spans and forming contribution triples, based on SemEval-2021 Task 11 (D'Souza et al.).
designs.task_name: NLPContributionGraph - Structured Extraction of NLP Contributions

designs.name: task01-codwoe
designs.title: CODWOE - Comparing Dictionaries and Word Embeddings
designs.description: Definition modeling for words in context, adapting SemEval-2022 Task 1 (CODWOE), which compared dictionary definitions with distributional word representations across two subtasks: definition modeling (embedding to definition) and reverse dictionary (definition to embedding). Based on Mickus et al.
designs.task_name: CODWOE - Comparing Dictionaries and Word Embeddings

designs.name: task02-idiomaticity
designs.title: Idiomaticity Detection
designs.description: Binary classification of whether a target multi-word expression is used idiomatically or literally in context, covering English and Portuguese. Based on SemEval-2022 Task 2 (Tayyar Madabushi et al.).

designs.name: task03-pretens
designs.title: PreTENS - Presuppositional Acceptability
designs.description: Judge the acceptability of sentences whose two nominal arguments are presupposed to stand (or not) in an ordered taxonomic relation. Includes a binary acceptable/unacceptable judgment and a 1-7 acceptability rating. Based on SemEval-2022 Task 3 (Zamparelli et al.).

designs.name: task04-patronizing-language
designs.title: Patronizing and Condescending Language Detection
designs.description: Detection and span-level identification of patronizing and condescending language directed toward vulnerable communities in news media. Based on SemEval-2022 Task 4 (Perez-Almendros et al.).

designs.name: task05-multimedia-misogyny
designs.title: SemEval-2022 Task 5: Multimedia Misogyny (MAMI)
designs.description: MAMI is the SemEval-2022 Task 5 benchmark for detecting misogynous memes from text and image content (Fersini et al.). This Potato config reproduces both subtasks: the binary misogyny label and the four-way misogyny type.

designs.name: task06-isarcasmeval
designs.title: iSarcasmEval: Intended Sarcasm Detection
designs.description: SemEval-2022 Task 6 (iSarcasmEval): detecting intended sarcasm in English and Arabic. Unlike prior datasets labeled by third parties, iSarcasmEval texts are labeled by their own authors for intended sarcasm. Annotators decide whether a text is sarcastic and, if so, which category of ironic speech it expresses.

designs.name: task07-plausible-clarifications
designs.title: Plausible Clarifications of Implicit and Underspecified Instructions
designs.description: Rate the plausibility of a candidate filler (clarification) for a gap in a wikiHow instructional text. Combines a multi-class judgment (IMPLAUSIBLE / NEUTRAL / PLAUSIBLE) with a graded 1-5 plausibility score. Based on SemEval-2022 Task 7 (Roth, Anthonio, and Sauer).

designs.name: task08-news-similarity
designs.title: Multilingual News Article Similarity
designs.description: Rating the similarity between pairs of news articles across seven dimensions (geography, entities, time, narrative, overall, style, tone), each on a 4-point scale, to assess whether they cover the same story across multiple languages. Based on SemEval-2022 Task 8 (Chen et al.).

designs.name: task09-r2vq-recipe-qa
designs.title: R2VQ - Recipe Question Answering
designs.description: Question answering over recipe texts, where annotators answer questions about recipes and classify whether the answer is explicitly stated, inferable, or not answerable from the recipe. A simplified adaptation of SemEval-2022 Task 9 (R2VQ, Tu et al.), whose original competence-based protocol answers template-based question families over recipes annotated with cooking-role and semantic-role layers.

designs.name: task12-symlink
designs.title: Symlink: Linking Mathematical Symbols to their Descriptions
designs.description: SemEval-2022 Task 12 (Symlink): extracting mathematical symbols and their textual descriptions from scientific documents and linking each symbol to the description it refers to. Annotators mark symbol and description spans, then link them with relation types (Direct, Count, Coref-Symbol, Coref-Description). Documents are drawn from arXiv papers across mathematics, physics, biology, economics, and computer science.

designs.name: task01-visual-wsd
designs.title: V-WSD - Visual Word Sense Disambiguation
designs.description: Visual word sense disambiguation task where annotators select the most appropriate image for a target word given its textual context. Based on SemEval-2023 Task 1 (Raganato et al.).

designs.name: task03-persuasion-news
designs.title: Detecting Persuasion Techniques in News
designs.description: Identification of propaganda and persuasion techniques in news articles through both multi-label classification and span-level detection. Based on SemEval-2023 Task 3 (Piskorski et al.).

designs.name: task04-valueeval
designs.title: ValueEval - Human Values behind Arguments
designs.description: Identification of human values expressed in arguments, classifying which of the Schwartz basic values an argument appeals to and whether it attains or constrains those values. Based on SemEval-2023 Task 4 (Kiesel et al.).

designs.name: task05-clickbait-spoiling
designs.title: Clickbait Spoiling
designs.description: Classification and extraction of spoilers for clickbait posts, including spoiler type identification and span-level spoiler detection. Based on SemEval-2023 Task 5 (Fröbe et al.).

designs.name: task06-legaleval
designs.title: LegalEval - Legal Document Analysis
designs.description: Understanding legal texts through the SemEval-2023 Task 6 (LegalEval) protocol: rhetorical role labeling of sentences, legal named entity recognition (L-NER) for entities such as courts, petitioners, respondents, judges, statutes, and precedents, and court judgment prediction with explanation. Based on SemEval-2023 Task 6 (Modi et al.).

designs.name: task07-clinical-trial-nli
designs.title: Clinical Trial NLI
designs.description: Natural language inference for clinical trial reports, determining whether a given statement is entailed or contradicted by clinical trial evidence. Based on SemEval-2023 Task 7 (Jullien et al.).

designs.name: task08-causal-medical-claim
designs.title: Causal Medical Claim Identification and PIO Frame Extraction
designs.description: Identify causal medical claim spans in Reddit health posts (Subtask 1: Claim, Experience, Experience-based claim, Question) and extract PIO frames — Population, Intervention, Outcome (Subtask 2). Based on SemEval-2023 Task 8 (Khetan et al.).
designs.task_name: Causal Medical Claim Identification and PIO Frame Extraction

designs.name: task09-tweet-intimacy
designs.title: Tweet Intimacy Analysis
designs.description: Rating the level of intimacy expressed in tweets on a 5-point scale, covering multilingual social media content. Based on SemEval-2023 Task 9 (Pei et al.).

designs.name: task10-explainable-sexism
designs.title: Explainable Online Sexism Detection
designs.description: Detection and fine-grained classification of online sexism with span-level evidence extraction. Categories include threats, derogation, animosity, and prejudiced discussion. Based on SemEval-2023 Task 10 (Kirk et al.).

designs.name: task12-afrisenti
designs.title: AfriSenti - African Language Sentiment
designs.description: Sentiment analysis for tweets in African languages, classifying text as positive, negative, or neutral. Covers 14 African languages including Amharic, Hausa, Igbo, Yoruba, and Swahili. Based on SemEval-2023 Task 12 (Muhammad et al.).

designs.name: task01-semantic-relatedness
designs.title: Semantic Textual Relatedness
designs.description: Semantic textual relatedness task requiring annotators to rate the degree of semantic relatedness between sentence pairs using both a Likert scale and a continuous slider. Based on SemEval-2024 Task 1 (STR).

designs.name: task02-safe-biomedical-nli
designs.title: Safe Biomedical NLI
designs.description: Safe biomedical natural language inference task requiring annotators to determine entailment or contradiction between statements and clinical trial report sections and provide reasoning. Based on SemEval-2024 Task 2 (NLI4CT: Safe Biomedical Natural Language Inference for Clinical Trials).

designs.name: task03-multimodal-emotion-cause
designs.title: Multimodal Emotion Cause Analysis
designs.description: Multimodal emotion cause analysis in conversations, requiring annotators to identify emotion expressions and their causal utterances in dialogue, and classify the emotion type. Based on SemEval-2024 Task 3.

designs.name: task04-persuasion-memes
designs.title: Persuasion Techniques in Memes
designs.description: Detection and classification of persuasion techniques in memes, requiring annotators to identify rhetorical and propaganda techniques in meme text and highlight persuasive spans. Based on SemEval-2024 Task 4.

designs.name: task05-argument-civil-procedure
designs.title: Argument Reasoning in Civil Procedure
designs.description: Legal argument reasoning task from SemEval-2024 Task 5. Given a short introduction to a U.S. civil procedure topic, a question, and a candidate answer (a possible solution argument), annotators perform binary classification: judge whether the answer candidate is correct (True) or incorrect (False). Questions and answers are drawn from a civil procedure textbook widely used in U.S. law schools.

designs.name: task07-numeval
designs.title: NumEval - Numeral-Aware Language Understanding and Generation
designs.description: Numeral-aware language understanding and generation across the five NumEval datasets: Quantitative Prediction (QP), Quantitative Natural Language Inference (QNLI), Quantitative Question Answering (QQA), reading comprehension of numerals (NQuAD), and numeral-aware headline generation (Num-HG). Based on SemEval-2024 Task 7 (NumEval).
designs.task_name: NumEval - Numeral-Aware Language Understanding and Generation

designs.name: task08-machine-generated-text
designs.title: Machine-Generated Text Detection
designs.description: Machine-generated text detection task requiring annotators to classify whether a given text was written by a human, generated by a machine, contains mixed authorship, or is uncertain. Based on SemEval-2024 Task 8.

designs.name: task09-brainteaser
designs.title: BRAINTEASER - Commonsense-Defying QA
designs.description: Lateral thinking and commonsense-defying question answering task requiring annotators to select answers to brain teasers that defy default commonsense assumptions and provide explanations. Based on SemEval-2024 Task 9 (BRAINTEASER).

designs.name: task10-emotion-flip
designs.title: Emotion Discovery and Reasoning its Flip
designs.description: Emotion discovery and flip reasoning task requiring annotators to identify the current emotion in a dialogue turn, and locate trigger spans and flip points where emotions change. Based on SemEval-2024 Task 10.
designs.task_name: Emotion Discovery and Reasoning its Flip

designs.name: task01-admire-multimodal-idiomaticity
designs.title: AdMIRe - Advancing Multimodal Idiomaticity Representation
designs.description: Multimodal idiomaticity task (SemEval-2025 Task 1, Subtask A): given a potentially idiomatic nominal compound in a context sentence, annotators rank five candidate images by how well each represents the sense in which the compound is used.

designs.name: task02-entity-aware-mt
designs.title: EA-MT - Entity-Aware Machine Translation
designs.description: Entity-aware machine translation evaluation requiring annotators to identify entity spans, classify translation errors, and provide corrected translations. Based on SemEval-2025 Task 2.

designs.name: task04-unlearning-sensitive-content
designs.title: Unlearning Sensitive Content from LLMs
designs.description: Evaluation of whether language models have successfully unlearned sensitive content, requiring annotators to assess model outputs for residual sensitive information leakage. Based on SemEval-2025 Task 4.

designs.name: task05-llms4subjects
designs.title: LLMs4Subjects - Subject Tagging for a Technical Library
